_source: NXT HCM Field Mapping 1.xlsx 'Source Files Mapping' GREEN rows, reconciled against HDL Template 3.xlsx and the real input INTXXX_CR_Oracle_Fusion_Demographic_V2 (31-Jul-2026)
_scope: Client NextPower · source system Workday · target object Employee HDL
_legend: The workbook's own legend: Green = Mapped, Yellow = Questions to NEXTPOWER, Orange = Duplicate, Blue = Oracle required but missing from source, Red = Not to Bring. Only GREEN is imported — read by CELL FILL (FF92D050) on the Source Column Name cell, not by eye. 20 of the 47 rows are green, and every one of them also reads 'Bring to Oracle = Yes'.
_column_spellings: The mapping tab writes source columns with UNDERSCORES (Employee_ID, Legal_First_Name) while the actual Workday extract header row uses SPACES (Employee ID, Legal First Name). Where the extract confirms a column, its REAL spelling is stored and the workbook spelling kept as an alias — the apply path resolves normalised, but the propagation path writes the stored value verbatim onto the mapping row, so storing the workbook spelling would leave a source column that does not exist in the dataset.
_scope_key: HDL 'sheets' in this tool are COMPONENT names (Location, Job, Position, PositionHierarchy, Worker, PersonName, PersonEmail, WorkRelationship, WorkTerms, Assignment, AssignmentSupervisor) — that is what hdl_seed_service writes one FBDISheet per. Scoping a learning to the top-level .dat object instead would exclude it from the component the field actually lives in: FirstName is on PersonName, not Worker. So hdl_components below is measured against hdl_schema.all_components(), and the workbook's own '(Object)' suffix is the narrowing key — EffectiveStartDate appears on NINE components, and the 1/1/1900 constant belongs to exactly two of them.

mappings.note: PersonName had no KnownAs attribute before this workbook; added to the loader schema so the green row has somewhere to land.
No (Object) suffix in the workbook, so it applies to every component that sources ActiveStatus. PositionHierarchy is excluded deliberately — there it is the constant 'A', not a mapped value.

The workbook names the COMPONENT (AssignmentSupervisor); the attribute is ManagerAssignmentNumber. It belongs to the SECOND Worker pass: a supervisor row points at the manager's assignment number, so every worker — managers included — must already exist. The real input carries a plain Manager_ID (944886 for employee 1007802), which the manager rule turns into E944886; the older 'Manager - Level 01' spelling holds a "Name (12345)" string and is kept as a fallback.

Mapping-file row 39: Cost_Center -> DefaultExpenseAccount, taken as written. The workbook's own TRX comment ('No suitable field is available in Oracle for this information') is contradicted by the client's HDL template, which carries DefaultExpenseAccount on Assignment — so the attribute exists (format, from the template) and it reads Cost_Center (mapping, from the mapping file). The template's cell shows a full accounting flexfield string; that is a SAMPLE, not a transformation invented here. Analyst, 31-Jul: 'treat template as purely a format in which FBDI downloads should happen, the inputs are for reference, check the mappings file for mapping and perform the mapping.'

Was also claimed on Assignment. The client's HDL template shows Assignment carrying DefaultExpenseAccount in that slot and no DepartmentName at all, so it lives on Position only — where the template shows 'Sales International', i.e. Cost_Center_Name.

Location code from Workday. Transformation logic may be applied to align with Oracle naming conventions (e.g., NXT_IND_HYD). Assignment also carries a LocationCode attribute, but the workbook's (Location) suffix scopes this to the Location component.
Job code from Workday. Transformation logic may be applied to align with Oracle naming conventions (e.g., NXT_SALES_DIR). Position and Assignment also carry JobCode; the (Job) suffix scopes this one.
Indicates whether the employee is currently on military service. Was hard-blank in the loader schema; now sourced, and still renders blank while the column is absent from the extract.
Position also carries a Name attribute; the workbook's (Job) suffix scopes this one to Job.

constants.note: Represents the effective start date of the location record in Workday. EffectiveStartDate exists on NINE components — unscoped, this constant would date-stamp every worker record 1900. The client's HDL template says 1990-01-01 where the mapping workbook writes '1/1/1900' — one digit apart, and the template is the artefact they load, so it wins.

Represents the effective start date of the job record in Workday. The client's HDL template says 1990-01-01 where the mapping workbook writes '1/1/1900' — one digit apart, and the template is the artefact they load, so it wins.

_hdl_objects: The five .dat files the generator writes, in load order: Location, Job, Position, PositionHierarchy, Worker. WorkRelationship is not a file — Worker.dat carries it as a child block — so hdl_object is the file and hdl_components are the blocks inside it.
_real_input: The tool is fed INTXXX_CR_Oracle_Fusion_Demographic_V2 — 23 columns, UNDERSCORED (Employee_ID, Job Code, Manager_ID), header on row 2 — NOT the 31-column 'Workday Extract' tab of the mapping workbook. All five columns previously flagged as coming from other Workday files (Manager_ID, Location_Code, Job_Code, Job Profile, Military_Service) are present in it. Column matching normalises punctuation, so underscore-vs-space resolves either way.
_authority: Two documents, two jobs. The HDL TEMPLATE is the FORMAT the download must take: which components exist, which attributes they carry, in what order, and the two-pass Worker split. Its sample VALUES are reference only — the company reads 'Nextpower LLC' where the real input says 'Nextracker LLC, USA'. The MAPPING FILE is the authority for which source column feeds which target field. Neither is used for the other's job.
